result:
The final answer of 1 is wrong, and so is the proposed solution's claim that no such k exists.

**k = 1 fails.** The block {1} has digit sum 1, which 2025 does not divide.

**The "none exist" claim fails.** Take m = 226, so 9m = 2034 ≥ 2024. Any block of 2·10^226 consecutive integers contains a complete aligned block {p·10^226, …, p·10^226 + 10^226 − 1}. In that block the digit sums are s(p) + t, where t is the digit sum of the last 226 digits. Every t from 0 to 2034 occurs, so the digit sums cover at least 2025 consecutive values. Some value in that range is a multiple of 2025. So a finite k does work, and a smallest one exists.

The proposed solution's argument for large k is also unsupported. It gives no real construction and only gestures at "advanced constructions."

The smallest k is some large finite number, not 1 and not "none."

VERDICT: REJECT
